statement: Define f(i) = receiver[i] for 0 <= i < n, with f^0(i) = i and f^(t+1)(i) = receiver[f^t(i)] for t >= 0. Define score(i) = sum_{t=0}^{k} f^t(i). The function returns a result r and r = max{ score(i) | 0 <= i < n }.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, get_max_function_value returns Ok r for some 64-bit integer r; it does not panic, return Err, perform an out-of-bounds access, or overflow the returned result.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: Define f(i) = receiver[i], f^0(i) = i, f^(t+1)(i) = receiver[f^t(i)], and score(i) = sum_{t=0}^{k} f^t(i). Whenever the function returns r, for every starting player i with 0 <= i < n, score(i) <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: Define f(i) = receiver[i], f^0(i) = i, f^(t+1)(i) = receiver[f^t(i)], and score(i) = sum_{t=0}^{k} f^t(i). Whenever the function returns r, there exists a starting player i0 with 0 <= i0 < n such that score(i0) = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r >= n - 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r <= (n - 1) * (k + 1).
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: If k = 1, then whenever the function returns r, r = max{ i + receiver[i] | 0 <= i < n }.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: If receiver is constant, meaning receiver[i] = receiver[0] for every i with 0 <= i < n, then whenever the function returns r, r = (n - 1) + k * receiver[0].
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = (n - 1) * (k + 1) if and only if receiver[n - 1] = n - 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: Let r1 be the result of get_max_function_value(receiver, k1) and r2 the result of get_max_function_value(receiver, k2). Whenever both calls return results r1 and r2, r1 <= r2.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 10^10.

statement: Let m = min{ receiver[j] | 0 <= j < n }. Whenever the function returns r, r >= (n - 1) + k * m.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: Let M = max{ receiver[j] | 0 <= j < n }. Whenever the function returns r, r <= (n - 1) + k * M.
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.

statement: If receiver[j] = j for some j with 0 <= j < n, then whenever the function returns r, r >= j * (k + 1).
preconditions: Let n = len(receiver). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= receiver[i] <= n - 1; and 1 <= k <= 10^10.
